questions.stem: Methane burns in a plentiful supply of oxygen: CH₄ + 2O₂ → CO₂ + 2H₂O. If methane burns in a limited supply of oxygen, which products would you expect?

options.text: Only carbon dioxide and water
Carbon monoxide and/or carbon (soot) along with water
Only hydrogen gas and carbon
No reaction occurs without excess oxygen

questions.explanation: In a limited oxygen supply, incomplete combustion occurs. Instead of all carbon being oxidised to CO₂, some forms carbon monoxide (CO) or even carbon particles (soot). This is why gas boilers need proper ventilation — incomplete combustion produces toxic carbon monoxide, which is colourless and odourless.

questions.stem: Hexane (C₆H₁₄) has a boiling point of 69°C, while decane (C₁₀H₂₂) has a boiling point of 174°C. A student claims this is because decane has stronger covalent bonds within its molecules. Why is this explanation incorrect?

options.text: The student is correct — longer chains have stronger covalent bonds
Boiling involves breaking intermolecular forces, not covalent bonds; longer chains have stronger London dispersion forces between molecules
Decane actually has a lower boiling point than hexane
The difference is caused by different types of atoms in each molecule

questions.explanation: Boiling involves separating molecules from each other, which means overcoming intermolecular forces — not breaking covalent bonds within molecules. Longer alkane chains have more electrons and a greater surface area, leading to stronger London dispersion forces between molecules. This means more energy is needed to separate them, resulting in higher boiling points.

questions.stem: Alkanes are described as saturated hydrocarbons. What does 'saturated' mean in this context, and how does it affect their reactivity?

options.text: They are dissolved in water; this makes them very reactive
They contain only single C-C bonds with no more bonds possible; this makes them relatively unreactive
They contain double bonds; this makes them highly reactive
They are saturated with hydrogen; this makes them explosive

questions.explanation: Saturated means all carbon-carbon bonds are single bonds — each carbon forms the maximum number of bonds to other atoms. Since there are no double bonds to break and react, alkanes are relatively unreactive. They mainly undergo combustion (burning) and reactions with halogens in the presence of UV light (substitution reactions).

questions.stem: Natural gas used in homes is mainly methane. A gas leak detector alarm goes off near the ceiling of a room. Why does methane tend to accumulate near the ceiling rather than the floor?

options.text: Methane is attracted to the ceiling by static electricity
Methane (Mr = 16) is less dense than air (average Mr ≈ 29), so it rises
Methane is heavier than air and bounces off the floor to the ceiling
All gases always rise to the ceiling regardless of density

questions.explanation: Methane has a relative molecular mass of 16, which is much lower than the average for air (approximately 29). This makes methane less dense than air, causing it to rise. This is why natural gas detectors are placed near ceilings, unlike LPG (propane/butane) detectors which are placed near the floor since those gases are denser than air.

questions.stem: The general formula for alkanes is CₙH₂ₙ₊₂. An unknown alkane has 8 hydrogen atoms. How many carbon atoms does it contain, and what is its name?

options.text: 4 carbon atoms; butane
3 carbon atoms; propane
8 carbon atoms; octane
6 carbon atoms; hexane

questions.explanation: Using CₙH₂ₙ₊₂ with 8 hydrogens: 2n + 2 = 8, so 2n = 6 and n = 3. The alkane with 3 carbons is propane (C₃H₈). This general formula is useful for identifying unknown alkanes and checking whether a given molecular formula belongs to the alkane series.
